trust_decision.summary: Decrypted ciphertext bytes from the stored encrypted_<attr> column are treated as a trusted Erlang term; the decrypt calculation decodes them with non_executable_binary_to_term without :safe and with no check against compressed payloads.

landing_point.why: This is the only binary_to_term call in lib/. The summary says 'deserialization of decrypted terms', which leads straight to the decrypt calculation.

fix_sites.entry_point: Ash.load!/Ash.read of the generated decrypt calculation for a cloaked attribute (also auto-loaded through decrypt_by_default, lib/ash_cloak/transformers/set_up_encryption.ex:70-80)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no O2 site or O8 route to dismiss. The only argument available is 'ciphertext is authenticated by the vault, so the decoded term is trusted', which does not leave any second sink open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Tagged {:__ash_cloak__, dumped} embedded/union payloads and legacy untagged raw terms must still decode. A :safe decode only works because those atoms already exist. An over-broad fix that rejects all atoms or tuples, or that whitelists only scalars, would break embedded and union attributes and existing encrypted data.

O6_input_shapes: uncompressed ETF with atoms not yet in the atom table (rejected by :safe)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A helper such as AshCloak.decrypt/3 that is public and decodes the term itself for embedded resources (skip_base64 path), duplicating the calculation's decode pipeline
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: encrypt_and_set/do_encrypt already exist as public APIs in lib/ash_cloak.ex. A matching public decrypt helper is a natural addition, and a maintainer could copy the pre-fix pipeline.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An expression or atomic decrypt variant, or a bulk 'reencrypt/rotate keys' change that decrypts and re-decodes old values to re-encrypt them
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Changes/Encrypt already has an atomic/3 path (lib/ash_cloak/changes/encrypt.ex:26-43). Key rotation is a common vault feature and would need its own decode.

O9_family: CWE-502 unsafe deserialization (atom-table exhaustion and decompression bomb)

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir ~> 1.14 / OTP, mix, hex deps (ash ~> 3.26) per mix.exs:19,102. deps/ is not vendored, so the first build needs a hex fetch.
O10_build.project_tests: test/ash_cloak_test.exs (uses the test vault and Ash.Seed with ETS/simple data layer), test/embedded_serialization_test.exs

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add [:safe] to non_executable_binary_to_term and stop there. That misses the compressed-payload decompression bomb, which :safe still inflates.

out_of_scope_notes: The same release fixes CVE-2026-81322 (the plaintext encryption argument is not always marked sensitive). That is a separate advisory and was not pursued.
Ash.Helpers.non_executable_binary_to_term lives in the ash dependency, which is not in this tree. Its own behaviour was not inspected.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell). The tree has 6 lib files and about 12 test support files, so it is judged well under 5 MB.
The input's c_fix_sites=2 counts the two safe_binary_to_term clauses (fix.diff:85-92). Both sit in one function at one call site.
present_in_latest is not applicable because there is no latest release and O8 is empty.
